title: Thai Peanut Chicken Crock
seoTitle: Thai Peanut Chicken Crock | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Slow-cooked peanut chicken with rice and bright vegetables
subtitle: Slow-cooked peanut chicken with rice and bright vegetables
description: Chicken thighs simmer in coconut-peanut sauce and are served with rice, lime, and crunchy vegetables.

steps.title: Morning start
steps.instruction: Place chicken thighs in the slow cooker, keeping the raw-chicken package away from ready-to-eat vegetables.

steps.title: Whisk sauce
steps.instruction: Whisk peanut butter, coconut milk, curry paste, soy sauce, and lime juice until smooth.

steps.title: Cook low
steps.instruction: Pour sauce over chicken, cover, and cook on low for 6 to 7 hours.

steps.title: Start rice
steps.instruction: Near dinner, cook rinsed rice covered so it is fresh when chicken is ready.

steps.title: Check chicken
steps.instruction: Check a thick thigh has reached 165°F before shredding or chopping it.

steps.title: Shred chicken
steps.instruction: Shred chicken in the sauce with two forks; do not remove all the cooking liquid.

steps.title: Adjust sauce
steps.instruction: Stir in hot water a little at a time if the peanut sauce is thicker than gravy.

steps.title: Prep cabbage
steps.instruction: Thinly shred cabbage and toss with lime and a pinch of salt just before serving.

steps.title: Hold hot
steps.instruction: Keep chicken on warm above 140°F and keep cabbage chilled until bowls are built.

steps.title: Serve bowls
steps.instruction: Portion rice, peanut chicken, cabbage, and lime wedges into each bowl.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-cook: turn off direct heat and cover Chicken thighs — hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven, never below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Log hold time on the pan with a grease pencil. If tones drop after service, cover hot food and keep sides on low heat or ice as appropriate. On return, spot-check proteins at safe internal temp before reopening the line.

steps.title: Pack down leftovers safely
steps.instruction: Cool Chicken thighs and hot components in shallow hotel pans within two hours — deep pots stay in the danger zone too long. Label with date; reheat proteins to 165°F minimum before second shift. Store cold components separately so textures survive overnight.

proTips: Use sunflower butter when peanut allergies require it.
Keep curry paste modest and offer heat separately.
Coconut milk may look separated; stir it smooth.
tonightSpread: Condiments: lime wedges, chili crisp, crushed peanuts
Set hot components closest to the crew; cold crunch and toppings at the far end of the line.
Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a run.
leftovers: Cool Chicken thighs in shallow pans within two hours; label with date and reheat to 165°F before second shift.
Store cold sides separately — hot and cold stacked overnight ruins texture.
whyCrewsLikeIt: The flavour develops while the crew works, while the vegetables remain fresh until dinner.
mealPrepNotes: Make-ahead: whisk sauce and shred vegetables 2 days ahead. Storage: refrigerate 3 days. Reheating: heat chicken to 165°F.
substitutions: Use almond butter for peanut butter.
